title: How much electrical energy does a lamp use?
goal: See how the electrical energy used by a lamp depends on its current and on how long it is lit.
note: The electrical energy a lamp uses is the potential difference across it times the current times the time it is lit.

graphs.title: The electrical energy rises in a straight line as the time increases.
graphs.label: Electrical energy

graphs.title: Drag the point along the graph to change the current and watch the electrical energy.
graphs.label: Electrical energy

sentences: The lamp is supplied by a 6 V battery.
The energy used is the potential difference times the current times the time.

predict.prompt: A lamp is lit for twice as long on the same battery with the same current. What happens to the electrical energy it uses?
predict.reveal: Make the time longer and watch the electrical energy.

concept_check.question: Which formula gives the electrical energy used by a lamp?
concept_check.explanation: Energy is the potential difference times the charge, and the charge is the current times the time, so E = V I t.

hints: The lamp changes electrical energy into light and heat.
Which two controls change the energy used?
Energy equals the potential difference times the current times the time.
